name: Exploitation for Client Execution

control.title: Separation of System and User Functionality

evidence.rationale: Applying current security updates to browsers, Office products, PDF readers, and other client applications reduces successful exploitation of known application vulnerabilities. Operating-system vulnerabilities and unknown application vulnerabilities require separate protections.

Remediating known vulnerabilities in browsers, Office products, PDF readers, and other client applications reduces successful exploit-based code execution. This does not prevent exploitation of unknown vulnerabilities or unremediated unsupported software.

Browsers and email clients are common targets for vulnerabilities that provide adversary code execution. Requiring the latest vendor-supported versions directly reduces exposure to known client-software vulnerabilities.
Uninstalling unnecessary browser or email-client plug-ins removes potential client-side exploitation targets.
Email sandboxing can detonate weaponized Office documents, PDFs, archives, and other attachments to identify exploit behavior before delivery.

Data execution prevention, control-flow protections, exploit guards, and similar mechanisms interfere directly with memory corruption and code execution in client applications. These features reduce the ability of an exploit to execute its payload.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.

ATLAS results describe the ATLAS release in versions.atlas, pinned by commit and digest. ATLAS changes often: a later release can add techniques and mitigations. An empty mitigation list means that this release links no mitigation, not that no mitigation exists. agent_related is derived by this project from names.
